title: Sam Altman at Startup School 2026: Why now is the best time to start a startup
summary: Altman argues that falling costs, short cycle times and AI agents make this the best moment ever to found a company. He advises holding contrarian conviction for years, finding a few believers, helping many people early, and ignoring cynics while building. He also covers AI safety and power concentration.

principles.text: Startups win when tech moves fast, costs fall and cycle times shrink; ecosystem shifts erode incumbent advantage.
principles.quote: the great startups tend to cluster when the ecosystem shifts and incumbents lose a lot of their advantage, and then also when you have these like cost and cycle time change.

principles.text: Find reasonable conviction in things conventional wisdom calls wrong, and be willing to be dismissed for years.
principles.quote: find the things. That you can develop like reasonable conviction in, that people decide the conventional wisdom is there just wrong, and be okay with it taking a long time

principles.text: Being doubted early is a gift: you get time to build without big competitors.
principles.quote: it was like an incredible gift because it meant we didn't have this like massive competitors and we had time to do our research and build our stuff and build our company.

principles.text: Be mildly helpful to many people; it compounds into unpredictable opportunities and co-founders.
principles.quote: find a way to be like mildly helpful to a lot of people.

principles.text: A clear vision with unclear first steps is fine, but you must still take imperfect steps to get data.
principles.quote: if the the kind of like highest level vision is clear, but the first few steps are very unclear, that's not a bad thing.

principles.text: Skip the sarcastic takes; pour energy into building, since cynicism is easy and creating value is hard.
principles.quote: you should like put all of your energy into building stuff and like resist the easy shots.
